rationale: C24 is a strong substantive and drafting precursor. It uses the same servicemember-voting framework: the Department of Defense works with States, defects in State voting laws require prompt correction, federal legislation may supplement State action, the Secretary of Defense should oversee continuing activity and report progress, and the ultimate purpose is protecting the voting rights of Armed Forces personnel. The child updates this machinery for the 1956 elections and redirects the principal appeal to Governors, while retaining Defense coordination and State cooperation. C05 shares the voting-rights and urgent-legislation rationale but lacks the child’s detailed federal-state administrative machinery. C06 parallels the Governor-addressed request and promised State Department assistance, but its different program and largely generic letter structure make it weaker.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Armed Services stand ready to give every assistance... effective opportunities for service people to vote overseas by State absentee ballot depends on close working cooperation between the Armed Services and the several States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Department of Defense is already working with State governments, and distributing to servicemen information on voting rights and procedures.
shared_material.explanation: Both establish Defense-State cooperation as the administrative mechanism for enabling servicemember voting.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hope that you will wish to have introduced and enacted in the 1955 Legislative Session of your State the uniform voting provisions above referred to... Therefore, I urge you to deal promptly with this matter
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It is important that officials in the States understand that action must be taken promptly to remedy defects in their State laws and procedures if servicemen from those States are to vote this year.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts the parent’s urgent appeal for corrective State legislation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am asking the Secretary of Defense to coordinate all activities of the Federal Government in the field of servicemen voting, and in due course he or his designee will directly offer to your State such cooperation and assistance as his office may be able to afford.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hope that you will continue to keep in touch with the States and the extent of progress which they make in improving soldier voting procedures... From time to time, I hope you will report to me on the progress which is being made in the field of soldier voting.
shared_material.explanation: The child converts the parent’s continuing Defense oversight and liaison role into an express coordination assignment.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the men and women who are defending our country all over the world
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the men and women of the armed forces will have the chance to exercise one of the great rights which they are now, in many cases, risking their lives to defend
shared_material.explanation: The shared rights-and-service formulation reinforces direct linguistic continuity beyond the common subject matter.
